chunks: From him, from Hakam Al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The female singer who attends the weddings, there is no problem with her earnings.
ai.seo_question: Is the income of a female wedding singer considered halal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the mere profession of a female singer (*al-mughanniya*) performing at weddings does not inherently invalidate her earnings. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the general permissibility of her income and the specific conditions of her performance, such as the absence of *lahw* (frivolous distraction) or *ghina'* (melodious singing) that leads to heedlessness of God.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Hakam Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The female singer who attends the weddings, there is no problem with her earnings’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the previous Hadith) from Hakam al-Hannat from abu Basir, who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam has said,
’The income of a female singer who attends wedding ceremonies is lawful.’”
